faces.f:
"Life, struck sharp on death, Makes awful lightning."
—Elizabeth Barrett Browning,
"Aurora Leigh"

"'Tis a shame, in such a tempest, to have but one anchor."
—Laurence Sterne, *Tristram Shandy*

"'O miserable of happy! Is this the end
Of this new glorious world... ?'"
—John Milton, *Paradise Lost*

"Let's do it again!"
—Squee, goblin cabin hand
They exist to cease.
Seeking the company of plants ensures that your wits will go to seed.

"She is a theme of honor and renown, . . . Whose present courage may beat down our foes."
—William Shakespeare, *Troilus and Cressida*
"Fools dig for water, corpses, or gold. The earth's real treasure is far deeper."
Meddling mages chant so loudly that no one can get a spell in edgewise.

"The tyrannous and bloody deed is done,
The most arch deed of piteous massacre
That ever yet this land was guilty of."
—William Shakespeare, *Richard III*

"All we know about the Krosan Forest we have learned from those few who made it out alive."
—Elvish refugee
The foolish wish for that which they desire. The cunning wish for that which they require.
Some convictions are so strong that the world must break to accommodate them.
...but the price of Mangara's freedom was Asmira's life.

"The land promises nothing and keeps its promise."
—Oracle *en*-Vec
In Lorwyn's brief evenings, the sun pauses at the horizon long enough for a certain species of violet to bloom with the fragrance of mischief.
A grave is the safest place to store ill-gotten treasures.
Greatness, at any cost.
"I wrecked your metal guy, boss. But look! I made you an ashtray."
"No single arrow can pierce an entire flock."
It is ancient, immense, and irresistible.
"Those who stood in my path now lay behind me."
Their fires burn quietly, allowing the phoenixes to glide silently through the canyon.
Not even the tallest tree stands a chance against the underside of a dinosaur's foot.

"Um...oh...what was I saying?"
—Reveka, wizard savant
"Patience, mage. Killing you now would be too easy."
Mastery is achieved when "telling time" becomes "telling time what to do."
"Allow me a moment to catch your breath."

"My favorite meal is angel's flesh, slain in agony and iced with black vinegar."
—Aszala of House Dimir

"Dangerous to recognize. Deadly not to."
—Lazav
"Fear not. Your life will not go unlived."

"Welcome to the Dimir Public Offices. Not responsible for death or loss of property. Basement off-limits."
—Sign outside Dinrova Building

"I am confident that if anyone actually penetrates our facades, even the most perceptive would still be fundamentally unprepared for the truth of House Dimir."
—Szadek

"Touched by moroii"
—Undercity slang meaning "to grow old"
The Gruul seek unbounded strength. The Dimir deliver cruel irony.
An emblem of a secret guild, the Dimir insignia is seen only by its own members—and the doomed.
The clouds grew thick, and then they grew teeth.
Izzet mages often acquire their magic reagents from dubious sources, so the potency of their spells is never predictable.
You don't so much hire goblins as put ideas in their heads.
He wants to watch Ravnica burn, one soul at a time.
Izzet brains and Izzet boilers: contents under pressure.
The Izzet learn something from every lesson they teach.

"Diametrically opposing energies in self-sealed plasmodermic bubbles make great pets!"
—Trivaz, Izzet mage

"Even this primitive specimen of my kind is impressive."
—Niv-Mizzet
To those in tune with the Firemind, there is no difference between knowledge and flame.
"The only action worth taking is one with an unknown outcome."
Quyzl was told by his mentor to "make more time" for his studies.
Tracing the horizon in a dance of wind and fire.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.
The outskirts of Golgari territory are guarded by more than just walls.
After fear and weakness rot away, that which remains is stronger than its living form.
Some Golgari insects live for centuries—and they never stop growing.
Cast out of the Conclave generations ago, these elves found a home in the corrupted districts of the Golgari.
The Izzet quickly suspended their policy of lifetime guarantees.
The rot farmer's first rite of passage is to craft a pair of work stilts.
Golgari reclaimers resent the gorgons, begrudging the loss of so many fine nutrients locked away in stone.

"Let the rest of Ravnica sneer. One way or another, they all end up in the undercity."
—Jarad
To the Golgari, anything buried is treasure.
He lurks in the undercity, eager for the corpse haulers to unload their rotting cargo.

"All matter, animate or not, rots when exposed to time. We merely speed up the process."
—Ezoc, Golgari rot farmer
"Nature's most raw beauty is the circle: perfect in its continuance, with no break between death and life."
Gorgons crave beautiful things: gems, exquisite amulets, the alabaster corpses of the petrified dead . . .
Depending on your point of view, the seal represents a proud guardian of the natural cycle or one who has sold her soul to darkness for eternal life.
Where Razia was aloof and untouchable, Aurelia is on the frontlines, calling for war.

"First, you must fight among the rank and file. It is there I will discern your skills as a leader."
—Aurelia, to Gideon Jura
"The hard part isn't landing in the saddle. The hard part is leaping before you see it."
"Subtlety is for lawmages and spies."
The upside to not thinking about the consequences is that you'll always surprise those who do.
Lieutenant Kos has never met a group of recruits he could not inspire or a mob he could not quell.

"Imagine a thunderstorm that's also a tactical genius. That's him."
—Dars Gostok, Firefist captain
When the Boros Legion attacks, swiftblades enter the fray first. They pick off the archers and mages, softening the enemy front before the flame-kin and giants go in.

"Let the pyres of the unbelievers light our way."
—Razia
Firemane Nevena led the victorious assault on the Barbu Rooftop rebels. Now the Gateless have marked her for death.
Though less well-known than its army of soldiers, the Boros Legion's mage-priests are as respected by the innocent as they are hated by the ghosts of the guilty.

"Yes, Boros tactics are unparalleled. But when your comrades are dying around you, inner strength must carry the day."
—Gideon Jura, to Aurelia
Her sword burns with such brightness that foes avert their eyes and arrows divert their paths.
Izzet-designed conductors atop Sunhome charge empty sets of armor that give form to the fluctuating elementals.

"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride."
—Agrus Kos
Sunhome—the stalwart shield, the towering sentinel, the seat of justice.
There are no soloists in the chorus of Selesnya.
Into the light the good are welcomed, and with the light the evil are banished.

"Ravnica, like a hedge, must be pruned, leaving only leaves of verdant uniformity."
—Niszka, Selesnya evangel
From the seeds of faith, great forests grow.
The consciousness of Mat'Selesnya does not always spread in peaceful ways.
No one in the Conclave acts alone.
Centaurs are sent to evangelize in Gruul territories where words of war speak louder than prayers of peace.
Instructors at the Kasarna training grounds are capable healers in case their students fail to grasp the subtleties of combat.
"We will defend the Worldsoul from Izzet 'progress' at any cost."
The righteous light of Selesnya is channeled through the devout, striking out to blind the nonbelievers.

"We will grow an army large enough to withstand the Izzet's madness."
—Trostani
"I have lived long, and I remember how this city once was. If my death serves to bring back the Ravnica in my memory, then so be it."

"We in the Conclave have a saying: 'When you hold a shield, lend your shield.' The strong must never forget what they owe to the weak."
— Niszka, Selesnya evangel
"The clamor of the city drowns all voices. But together we can sing a harmony that will resonate from Ravnica's tallest spires to her deepest wells."

"One day every pillar will be a tree and every hall a glade."
—Trostani
Only in Ravnica do the wolves watch the flock.
The symbol of the Conclave is one of unity, with tree supporting sun and sun feeding tree.
"I serve only justice. But through that duty, I serve all of Ravnica."

"As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable."
—Augustin IV
"Your potential to commit a crime warrants further investigation."
"Life is fleeting, and so is death. Only the oath is eternal."
As whispers and rumors increased, so did the demand for fail-safe barriers.

"I never thought I'd be so glad to see two tons of beak and claws bearing down on me at the speed of an arrow."
—Mirela, Azorius hussar

"It misses nothing and it has no sense of humor."
—Barvisa, courtroom scribe
"We have confiscated your spells as evidence. Once we conclude our investigation, you may petition to have them returned."

"Try not to look guilty. Or delicious."
—Thorpe, street urchin
"Let the knowledge of absolute law inspire you to live a life of absolute order."

"The higher the mind soars, the greater its understanding of the law."
—Isperia
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
"Spend your life betraying me if you wish. I'll simply take it up with your ghost."
Rakdos cultists hanged her for sport in the township square. Her ghost now stands vigil at what has become known as the Tree of Weeping.
Her cold wail echoes in the alleys and under-eaves, finding the unfortunate and turning their blood to ice.

"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies."
—Savra

"Let him be an example to others who would default on their debts to us."
—"The Cozen," Orzhov assassin

"I feel in them a sense of duty and commitment, yet I can feel nothing else. It is as if their duty is to an empty void."
—Razia
One moment, conscious only of a sense of repose. The next moment, hearing the trudge of his own footsteps. He sighed and squinted into the glare ahead.
Which is worse—the sleep which never ends or that which never comes?
"That must weigh heavily on your soul. Let me purge it for you."
The form of the sigil is just as important as the sigil itself. If it's carried on a medallion, its bearer is a master. If it's tattooed on the body, its bearer is a slave.
As the bounty on Massacre Girl rose, so did the number of imitators.

"I like a little entertainment with my dinner."
—Rakdos
The mask isn't meant to hide his identity. It's meant to keep the viscera out of his eyes.
The fear of dragons is as old and as powerful as the fear of death itself.

"Finally, a weapon the Boros can't confiscate!"
—Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
Such is the power of Rakdos that even his shadow takes on a cruel life of its own.
Its favorite treats are candied hands and sweet hearts.
In Rakdos-controlled neighborhoods, everyone is part of the show.
Few puppets are so willing.
Sacrificial rites take place before an audience of cheering cultists, each begging to be the next on stage.
Devil-blades and dripping blood make music Rakdos never tires of hearing.
"If there were such a thing as a soul, I think it would be behind the gallbladder but above the kidneys."
When Lord Rakdos stirred from his slumber, everyone else's nightmare began.
Most auramancers would have let the spikes hover just above the skin. Having the spikes rip through the skin from beneath was a touch added by Rakdos himself.
Rakdos festivals almost leave enough rubble in their wake to hide the bodies.
The Rakdos use it for everything you can think of and plenty more than that.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
Long ago, birds of paradise littered the skies. Thanks to the city's sprawl, most now exist as pets of society's elite.

"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!"
—Borborygmos

"The Gruul embrace all things poisonous and living in the cracks of society."
—Teysa Karlov
Some use magic to spy through walls. Others use it to crush them.

"It's easy to see why those Gruul dirtbags follow him—the only orders he gives are 'Crush them!' and 'We eat!'"
—Teysa Karlov
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.
Gruul shamans are bent on punishing the civilized. Any act more complex than rubbing sticks together or eating with utensils is met with the stinging burn of their magic.

"The Simic come from the cold slow depths. How could they understand the fire in a wild heart?"
—Kroshkar, Gruul shaman

"We respect all lifeforms, but this one we respect from a distance."
—Mandor, Selesnya ranger

"Not Gruul? Then die!"
—Borborygmos

"All the coins in Ravnica can't save his soul now."
—Narbulg Nine Fingers

"This city will perish, and the Gruul will cheer as the boar-god crushes the last bricks into dust."
—Nikya of the Old Ways
The Orzhov contract the Izzet to animate slum districts and banish them to the wastes. The Gruul adopt them and send them back to the city for vengeance.

"Nature is the ultimate mindless destroyer, capable of power and ferocity no army can match, and the Gruul follow its example."
—Trigori, Azorius senator
They inflict pain to forget their own and break foes to feel whole.
"Only the decadent think magic should be pristine and without cost."
Gurley was the first to domesticate one, though his widow didn't take much solace in that accomplishment.
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.

"We've merged your life essence with that of several creatures at once. You're welcome."
—Speaker Trifon

"We paid the Simic very well for this capability, but we should quickly recoup our expenses in saved wages."
—Milana, Orzhov prelate
It grows to hate you.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.

"Of course it will grow beyond control—it was designed to choose its own evolution."
—Momir Vig
The Simic soon discovered that the sky offered as few constraints on size as the sea.

"This creature has hyperevolved chameleonic abilities. It no longer mimics its surroundings, instead forcing them to take on its form."
—Simic research notes

"We've bred out the shortcomings of the species' natural form and replaced them with assets of our own design."
—Momir Vig
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.

"It is technically an ooze, but its life span measures only seconds. In that short time, its appetite for magic is extraordinary."
—Simic research notes
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
Once the felidar has marked you as prey, there's no point in running.
"I would be a fool if I taught you everything I know."
"We share a common enemy. Does that not make us friends?"
Half the size, double the mayhem.
"Come, my wild children. Let's give the interlopers a woodland welcome."
She had not believed any shred of humanity remained in these writhing monsters until the twisted form of her partner appeared before her.
Kytheon and his irregulars worked outside the law to bring justice to the streets of Akros.
"I feel the presence of the God-Pharaoh in the Second Sun, and I rise upon its rays."
"Bant's most gallant knights wear my sigil, and for that I am humbled."
Sometimes gestures of support are small. Sometimes not.
"Your death will be a balm, your passing a welcome revision, and all will sigh with peace to know of your demise."
"My scars are my sigils. I will wear them with pride long after you're gone."
The sky takes flight and the earth trembles.
"My skill sharpens with each beat of my wings."
Six feet of earth muffled his cries.
It slithers through the senses, constricting consciousness and poisoning perceptions.

"Eyes see only what is possible. A trained mind can explore the impossible."
—Kefnet, god of knowledge

"Nobody asked you to butt in, Jace. But thanks."
—Chandra Nalaar

"The tides have begun to ignore the moon."
—Tamiyo's journal
Strong wings make strong winds.

"Dear brother, it's sweet that you have chosen to share your toys with Ludevic, but I too have found some new playmates."
—Ghoulcaller Gisa
Carefully following the thaumatic compass Bolas had given her, Vraska blundered straight into the River Heralds' trap.
The greatest treasure of the deep is an echo from above.
The banished have come home to roost.

"We entered the church in search of solace, but it became clear we wouldn't find it there."
—Grete, Order of Saint Traft

"I welcome the use of even the foulest magic if it will rid us of the monstrosities that plague our world."
—Munda, ambush leader
"There are so many of them. It seems they've just been waiting for someone to serve."
The Curse of Wandering leaves only hatred.

"Death is no excuse for disobedience."
—Liliana Vess
The dead who wander beyond the safety of the city crave only to spread their curse.
It's not the size of the rock. It's how badly you want to lift it.

"I don't think they'll appreciate my . . . adjustments."
—Karavin, renegade saboteur
Dragon birth lairs are littered with treasure to entice the young from their eggs.
"Only those who give the dragons the respect they deserve may bear our title."
To wield lightning is to tame chaos.
Fools believe that Kolaghan's brood follows lightning storms. The wise know that it is the other way around.
"I have yet to find my equal."
The God-Pharaoh's most devoted took it upon themselves to follow his example.

"Our survival, like theirs, depends on our ability to work together."
—Huatli, to Tishana
The earth walks, strongest of all.
Often found browsing on the upper canopies of Ixalan's jungles, whiptails are known to absently bat away anything foolish enough to interrupt their meal.
They cover their territory like a tide of teeth and claws.
Raptors are clever enough to tear away a hard metal shell to get at the tasty morsel inside.

"Nobody's seen the Lady of Videns for years. Poor dear, no companions at all in that old castle."
—Yonda of Gavony
The herds follow as new growth arises.

"It appears that nature has risen against us."
—Captain Brinely Rage
It wails of buried riches and the souls lost seeking them.
Armored in courage and armed with searing light, her legion stands unflinching against the forces of darkness.
Her haunting tune drowns out the percussion of snapping masts.
A despot in life. A monster in death.
"Glory to the Burning Ones! May their mighty fangs devour all foes!"
The elvish kingdoms of Llanowar are united in their distrust of outsiders.
"Oathbreaker, I cast you out!"
"I will protect the less fortunate. I will love bravely. I will face despair and fight on. As a Capashen, I can do no less."
"You will respect the dead."
Carving lines through the sky, kite sailors map trails for the pilgrims below to follow.
"Swords cannot reach far enough. Chains cannot strike hard enough. An eternal dilemma, but a simple one."
"We take only what we need to survive. Believe me, you will need this."
The angel remembers her past lives like dreams. Her song held up meadows. Her blade drove back darkness. Her wings carried her across the ages.

"We fight not for Avacyn, but for her ideals; not for the church, but for its people."
—Thalia, Guardian of Thraben
"The arc of my blade has carved a path of light for the peace that will follow."

"Every choice alters the path of fate."
—Sarkhan Vol

"I prefer loyalty to be a matter of respect, not of magic. But one does what one must."
—Kaalia of the Vast
From the time they are hatchlings, river drakes are taught to pull the largest prey from the Luxa.
It is ancient, immense, and irresistible.
"I always attack from where their spyglasses can't see."
"Try to pretend like you understand what's important."

"The union of sea and sky makes a perfect cover."
—Talrand, sky summoner

"Violence is the food it craves. Feed it if you dare."
—Doriel, mentor of Mistral Isle
"You call it luck. I call it preparation."
Mklthd had always hated crowds . . . and they had always hated him.
Rumors float through the city like crows, alighting on citizens seemingly at random.
"To control the present we must master the future."

"I do things in my own time."
—Etha, initiate of Rhet crop
"You aren't invited."

"Virtue is virtue, whatever the heart that nurtures it."
—Malacan, Vantress exile
"The secret entrance should be near."
After Talrand conquered the depths of Shandalar, his ambitions drove him skyward, joined by servants whose drive and curiosity equaled his own.

"Soaring is wasted on the winged."
—Edric, Spymaster of Trest
Blood seeps into the stone, and darkness emerges.
"If you've never feasted on Zagoth terror-pig, I got the best price you'll find."
Hatred is a potent ally, but an insatiable master.

"An angel can shine like the sun, inspire the weak, and even threaten victory over darkness. But in the end it matters not, for it still dies like any other pest."
—Ob Nixilis
There is only one fate left to those banished from the God-Pharaoh's city.
Once they reached Orazca, the Legion's explorers ransacked tombs and temples, hunting for the Immortal Sun.
Grixis is a world where the only things found in abundance are death and decay. Corpses, whole or in part, are the standard currency among necromancers and demons.

"We entered the church in search of solace, but it became clear we wouldn't find it there."
—Grete, Order of Saint Traft
A few aetherborn have discovered a way to sustain their own existences at the cost of an insatiable hunger for the life essence of other beings.
It glides on silent wings across the midnight sky, and a dread host rises to follow.
"There are so many of them. It seems they've just been waiting for someone to serve."
The Curse of Wandering leaves only hatred.

"Who am I to break up a family?"
—Ghoulcaller Gisa
For a ghoul, every village is a buffet and every disaster is a reunion.
Some will sacrifice everything for but a taste of power.
Opening Orazca unleashed more horrors than just the Immortal Sun.

"They may show up with the wrong thigh bone or mandible, but they always show up."
—Zul Ashur, lich lord

"It's always my brightest students who make the worst decisions."
—Shaile, Silverquill dean

"All are not equal—neither in life nor after death. Bontu's favorites will stand highest in eternity."
—Senifet, vizier of Bontu
"You can sign, or you can spend your life imagining what might have been yours."
The Skelle raise scorn poles in conquered villages—cursed totems of wood and bone that sap survivors of physical strength and the will to fight back.

"Peace is a privilege you haven't earned."
—Tevesh Szat
The desert is a voracious beast, devouring both flesh and stone.
When a dragon attacks, there are no bystanders.
Fire never dies alone.

"The dragon is a perfect marriage of power and the will to use it."
—Sarkhan Vol
Dragon birth lairs are littered with treasure to entice the young from their eggs.

"Those dragons grow fast. For a while they feed on squirrels and goblins and then suddenly you're missing a mammoth."
—Hurdek, Mazar mammoth trainer
"You'll bend to my will—with or without your precious sanity."
"We speak the dragons' language of flame and rage. They speak our language of fury and honor. Together we shall weave a tale of destruction without equal."

"Spread out, you idiots! Spread out!"
—Marsden, party leader, last words
He marks his territory with fire and wrath, etching the mountainside with his charring breath.

"For dim-witted, thick-skulled genetic mutants, they have pretty good aim."
—Sisay
Baby dragons can't figure out humans—if they didn't want to be killed, why were they made of meat and treasure?
Small words stoke large flames.
"Only those who give the dragons the respect they deserve may bear our title."
It woke to find a vast world in need of a master.
The sparkmage shrieked, calling on the rage of the storms of his youth. To his surprise, the sky responded with a fierce energy he'd never thought to see again.
The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.

"Surely it won't notice if I take—"
—Theria the Sly, last words
"Grab what you want and burn the rest. Leave nothing behind."

"It's just playing with us, Marsden."
—Dafynne the Radiant, last words

"For all I have lost, for all who have fallen, I will render you to dust."
—Jared Carthalion
"The tiniest mouse speaks louder to me than all the festival crowds on Tin Street."

"Fynn climbed the highest peak and waited, still and silent, until the falling snow had hidden him entirely. When the great eagle flew past, the hunter's aim was true."
—Saga of the Wisdom Seeker
Call one, call them all.

"No elf can match a Tuskeri in combat. Why not charge?"
—Knorjolvin, Tuskeri raider
"The elves tend the forest, and the forest sustains the elves. My role is to ensure that the cycle continues."
The spires of Ravnica are no different from the tall trees of other planes. The elves navigate and protect them just the same.
"From a tiny sprout, the greatest trees grow and flourish. May the seeds of your mind be equally fruitful."

"Smash this city to pieces."
—Domri Rade
Elves of the immaculate class weave flora into living creatures—sometimes to endorse an elite warrior, sometimes to create a breathing work of art.
"If you only follow where the paths lead, you merely go where others have gone before you."
As patient and generous as life, as harsh and merciless as nature.
"Llanowar remembers the Ice Age, the Phyrexian Invasion, and the Rift Era. So long as we draw breath, we will ensure such disasters never threaten our world again."
Nature doesn't walk.
A healthy felidar is voracious yet regal. A rabid felidar is nothing more than appetite lashed to frothing jaws.

"Need a medic! And some stonemasons!"
—Wyllon, Drannith merchant
While the root remains, the tree yet lives.
The safety of the village depends on the beast thinking with its stomach.
Their arrows are tipped with basilisk eyes and fletched with cockatrice feathers.

"Savagery is the birthright of every creature that draws breath—or wishes it could."
—Karador, Ghost Chieftain
"Though you may leave this haven we have found, may our strength never leave you."
Mirrodin's creator still lives, still shapes metal, and still commands world-shaking power.
The weapon wields the hand that holds it.
"There's only one way to be sure it's really dead."
The only blow that matters is the killing blow.
It wails of buried riches and the souls lost seeking them.
When wielded by a true believer, it matters little whether the sword is a relic or a replica.

"Until this expedition is done, that blade is your guardian, your liberator, and your best friend all rolled into one."
—Yon Basrel, Oran-Rief survivalist

"We pray to Avacyn on high.
On snow-white wings fearless you fly.
Keep safe our souls. Keep safe our lives.
May angels watch us from the skies."
—Children's prayer

"Some aspire to climb the mountain of Honor. The Benalish are born upon its peak, and from there ascend among the stars."
—*History of Benalia*
Vampires know blood and the systems that carry it. And they know exactly where to strike to set it free.
Benalish citizens born under the same constellations share a star-clan. Their loyalty to one another interlaces the Seven Houses.

"Undefeated in battle, she is the shining future our empire deserves."
—Huatli
Rest sometimes requires the right prompting.

"For the lands you have lost and the beauty that remains, for freedom and the future, we must hold nothing back!"
—Gideon Jura
"Our enemies will soon discover that we are not as meek as they had believed."
The unicorns of Sursi are a manifestation of Serra's joy and compassion. They frolic and dance like children, offering blessings to anyone they encounter.
The angel remembers her past lives like dreams. Her song held up meadows. Her blade drove back darkness. Her wings carried her across the ages.
The remnants of Innistrad's corrupted angelic hosts collapsed to form the Flight of Nightmares.

"Improvement is a consequence of practice."
—Stitcher Geralf
Pray that it doesn't seek the safety of your lungs.
Six feet of earth muffled his cries.

"Like ribbons of wind and wisdom the coatls fly, twisting mystery into truth, shaping the clouds to suit their inscrutable will."
—Huatli

"I don't need your mage-rings or your mana equations. I call, and the sea answers."
—Keyta, rebel hydromancer
Progress comes at a price.
He grants endless wishes, as long as you always wish for a blade.
"I do as I please, little mortal. Do go on about your wishes, though—they amuse me to no end."
Vastly outnumbered, the Zendikari found creative ways to even the odds.
On Innistrad, Liliana embraced necromancy, honing her powers by practicing on scores of undead—and sometimes the living.
Grixis is a world where the only things found in abundance are death and decay. Corpses, whole or in part, are the standard currency among necromancers and demons.
